original_value: AbstractThe primary aim of this preliminary study is to examine a possible association between interest and mathematics performance among Malaysian students in a technology-enhanced learning environment. The Mathematics Interest Inventory was administered to 40 students to measure students’ interest towards mathematics, while a mathematics test was used to measure students’ mathematics performance. Results of the descriptive statistical analyses revealed that the students were relatively interested in mathematics. Correlational analyses showed that interest was not significantly correlated to mathematics performance among the students. Nevertheless, a significant relationship between interest and mathematics performance was found among students who had lower mathematics performance. The findings of this study pointed to the importance of igniting interest among students with lower mathematics performance given its strong link to mathematics performance. The Interest-Driven Creator theory served as an anchor in the theoretical framework of the study and it was discussed within the context of mathematics learning.

result.paraphrase: This preliminary study aimed to investigate a possible link between interest and mathematics performance among Malaysian students in a technology-enhanced learning setting. To gauge students’ interest in mathematics, the Mathematics Interest Inventory was given to 40 students, and a mathematics test was used to assess their performance. Descriptive statistics showed that the students were relatively interested in mathematics. Correlational analysis indicated that interest was not significantly related to mathematics performance overall. However, a significant relationship between interest and mathematics performance emerged among students with lower mathematics performance. The findings highlight the importance of fostering interest in students with weaker mathematics performance because of its strong association with mathematics achievement. The study’s theoretical framework was anchored by the Interest-Driven Creator theory, which was discussed in the context of mathematics learning.
